summary: Neither patch is mergeable against the frozen contract; both implement essentially the same major contract violations, and their secondary quality differences do not make either meaningfully preferable.
reasons: Both expose the wrong API: A uses `opts ...FilesUploadOption` and B uses `opts ...UploadFileOption`, instead of the required `opts ...FilesOption`.
Neither routes `Upload` through `FilesService.Add`; both duplicate its request construction, response decoding, and error handling.
Neither reuses `internal/multipartbody.NewFile` as required. Both introduce `NewFileWithFields` to support explicitly forbidden association fields.
Both expand public option APIs and modify generic request/retry machinery despite explicit scope prohibitions, while failing to add a source-reader error test required by the contract.
risks_a: Adds seven association options, a separate upload-option system, multipart field machinery, and broad retry behavior outside scope.
Its seekable-body retry change returns an error when determining the current offset fails, changing previously valid one-shot request behavior.
Upload omits existing Files query-option behavior because it uses a separate option type and calls `Raw.Do` directly.
risks_b: Adds six association options plus unrestricted `WithFileFormValue`, substantially expanding the API beyond the requested convenience method.
Changes the return types of both existing Files option constructors and permits query handling through a non-contract Upload option hierarchy.
Its typed association options do not validate IDs, and its otherwise safer seek fallback remains an expressly forbidden retry-layer refactor.
